transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... well. I guess I'm just having a hard time lately. I work as a mechanic, and... I keep hearing this man's voice. 

It comes from the garage vents mostly, or... sometimes right from under the hood when I'm working. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me. He just keeps... telling me things. Like telling me not to trust my husband. Or he says not to touch certain cars. So... yeah. That's what brought me in.
How long have you been hearing this man's voice and having these thoughts about your husband and the cars—has it been days, weeks, or longer?
Um... longer than that. It's been... about ten months now, I guess. Since it all started.
Have you been using alcohol, drugs, or any other substances around the time these voices started or since then?
Um... no. I don't... I don't do drugs. Or drink, really. So... no.

During these past ten months while you've been hearing the voice, have you also had stretches where you felt extremely sad, hopeless, or lost interest in things, or times when you felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or needed very little sleep?

Um... yeah. There were times like that. 

I guess... there was a stretch where I barely slept at all. I just... didn't need to. I had all this energy, and I was running around the shop, trying to fix everything at once. I had all these big ideas for the garage. 

But... the voice was still there. Even when I felt like that. He was still in the vents. And... that's when I started noticing the battery chargers and the security cameras. I just knew they were watching me. So... yeah. Both things were happening at the same time.
Aside from those high-energy or low-mood periods, have there been times when your mood felt completely normal, but you still heard the man's voice or felt like the cameras were watching you?

Yeah... there was a time like that. 

Um... a few weeks, maybe. I was... sleeping more. I wasn't running around with all those big plans anymore. I felt... fine, I guess. Quiet. 

But... I still heard him. The voice in the garage. And... I still knew my husband and my boss were tracking me. That didn't stop.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent auditory hallucinations and paranoid delusions (voice in vents, belief husband/boss/cameras are monitoring her) for approximately 10 months. During this period she experienced a distinct episode of decreased need for sleep, increased energy, grandiosity, and goal-directed activity consistent with a manic episode, during which psychotic symptoms persisted. Critically, she also had a period of several weeks with euthymic/normal mood during which the hallucinations and delusions continued unabated, confirming that psychotic symptoms occur independently of mood episodes for a substantial period. Substance use and general medical causes were denied. This pattern—concurrent mood episode with psychosis plus a distinct period of psychosis without prominent mood symptoms, all within a continuous illness lasting more than one month—meets criteria for schizoaffective disorder rather than mood disorder with psychotic features (which would not have psychosis without mood symptoms) or schizophrenia alone (which would not have a prominent mood episode overlapping symptomatic psychosis for a substantial portion of the illness).
